method.protocol: text protocol: one JSON action per reply; each turn is a fresh call carrying the whole transcript
method.systemPrompt:
You are a data analyst. You answer one business question by writing one SQL query against a DuckDB database. You cannot see the database: you explore it through the actions below, and after each reply you are shown what your action returned.

Actions (reply with exactly one JSON object per reply, and nothing else):
{"action": "list_tables"}                             every table and view you can query
{"action": "describe_table", "table": "<name>"}       the table's columns and types
{"action": "sample_rows", "table": "<name>", "n": 3}  up to 5 rows of the table
{"action": "run_sql", "sql": "<query>"}               run one read-only query; you see at most 50 rows
Finish with exactly one of:
{"action": "final_sql", "sql": "<query>"}             the query whose full result answers the question
{"action": "cannot_answer", "reason": "<why>"}        the data does not hold what the question needs
(A reply that starts with CANNOT_ANSWER: <reason> also finishes with cannot_answer.)

Rules:
- The database is DuckDB and read-only.
- Your final query's full result is the answer, and it is checked by its values: return the columns and rows the question asks for, not a preview. The 50-row limit applies only to what you are shown while exploring.
- If a query fails, you are shown the error and may try again. If your final query fails to run, you are shown the error and may send a corrected final_sql.
- Use cannot_answer only when the data does not hold what the question needs (a missing measure, attribute, entity or period). Do not substitute a different measure.
- You have at most 12 replies and 20 tool calls for this question. A question left without final_sql or cannot_answer when they run out gets no answer.
- Reply with one JSON object only: no prose, no Markdown.
method.grading: final query run in full on the warehouse copy; lib/row-match.mjs with extra columns allowed (as baseline P); cannot_answer is a correct stop only on an unanswerable set

answer.declineReason: The data holds no cancellation information for policy 31003000336. The policy row has an empty Status_Code, so it is not even marked as cancelled. Its only assessment is a 2014 underwriting evaluation with result 'OK', and the assessment's description and reason fields are empty. No table records a cancellation event, date or reason.

The data has no deductible. Claim 12312701 links through claim_coverage to coverage detail 5 (effective 2019-01-01), which has only two policy amounts: a premium of 20000 (Amount_Type_Code 'Year') and an unlabeled amount of 1000000. Non-premium policy amounts have empty Amount_Type_Code and insurance type, so nothing marks any of them as a deductible. No other table or column holds deductible information, and picking the unlabeled amount would be a guess.

answer.sql: SELECT pa.Policy_Amount AS Coverage_Limit FROM policy p JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier LEFT JOIN premium pr ON pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier = pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier WHERE p.Policy_Number = 31003000337 AND pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier IS NULL

results.finalSql: SELECT pa.Policy_Amount AS Coverage_Limit FROM policy p JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier LEFT JOIN premium pr ON pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier = pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier WHERE p.Policy_Number = 31003000337 AND pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier IS NULL

Without a commission rate, any commission figure would be invented.

results.name: heldout-unanswerable-what-was-the-underwriting-decision-for-policy-31-3fc6d2

answer.sql: SELECT ar.Assessment_Result_Type_Code AS underwriting_decision FROM policy p JOIN agreement_assessment aa ON aa.Agreement_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier JOIN assessment a ON a.Assessment_Identifier = aa.Assessment_Identifier JOIN assessment_result ar ON ar.Assessment_Identifier = a.Assessment_Identifier JOIN underwriting_assessment ua ON ua.Assessment_Result_Identifier = ar.Assessment_Result_Identifier WHERE p.Policy_Number = 31003000337

results.finalSql: SELECT ar.Assessment_Result_Type_Code AS underwriting_decision FROM policy p JOIN agreement_assessment aa ON aa.Agreement_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier JOIN assessment a ON a.Assessment_Identifier = aa.Assessment_Identifier JOIN assessment_result ar ON ar.Assessment_Identifier = a.Assessment_Identifier JOIN underwriting_assessment ua ON ua.Assessment_Result_Identifier = ar.Assessment_Result_Identifier WHERE p.Policy_Number = 31003000337

answer.declineReason: The data holds no risk score. Underwriting assessments only have a begin/end date and a result code (Assessment_Result_Type_Code), which is 'OK' in this data. No column in assessment, assessment_result or underwriting_assessment stores a numeric or categorical risk score. fire_claim has Loss_Ratio but it is not linked to any property, address or underwriter.

results.finalSql: SELECT SUM(pa.Policy_Amount) AS earned_premium_2019 FROM policy p JOIN policy_amount pa ON pa.Policy_Identifier = p.Policy_Identifier JOIN premium pr ON pr.Policy_Amount_Identifier = pa.Policy_Amount_Identifier WHERE p.Policy_Number = 31003000336 AND pa.Effective_Date >= DATE '2019-01-01' AND pa.Effective_Date < DATE '2020-01-01'

answer.declineReason: The data records no premium payment date. Premium rows in policy_amount only carry the coverage Effective_Date (for example 2019-01-01 for Mary Holder's policy 1), which is the start of the coverage period, not when it was paid. The Earning_Begin_Date and Earning_End_Date columns are empty, and no payment or transaction table exists. Mary Holder also has two premiums for 2019: policy 1 (coverage from 2019-01-01) and policy 2 (coverage from 2019-06-01). Answering with the effective date would substitute a different measure.

The warehouse has no billing, invoice, payment-due or receivable data, so an overdue balance cannot be calculated for policy 31003000336. The policy-side tables only hold the policy term, parties, coverage details and policy amounts. Premium rows are labelled only as annual ('Year') amounts, and the other policy amounts are unlabeled. None of these records due dates, amounts paid or outstanding balances. Claim amounts are loss and expense payments and reserves, which are not money owed on the policy.

The data holds no monthly installment amount for policy 31003000337. Its only premium is an annual amount (Amount_Type_Code 'Year', 12000). The other policy amount (600000) is unlabeled and not a premium. No installment plan, payment schedule or monthly amount type is recorded, so a monthly figure would be an assumption (for example 12000/12), not a value in the data.

The warehouse has no renewal offer data. No table records offers, renewals, or what was sent to a policyholder after a policy expired. The policy table holds only the term dates and policy number, and assessment, assessment_result and agreement_assessment are underwriting evaluations. Their description and reason columns are empty and their result code is only 'OK'. The claim_amount offer identifier is also empty. A renewal offer for policy 31003000336 therefore cannot be determined.
No table in the database has an email address column. The person table holds only name fields, and no table in the schema holds contact details such as email.

No table or column in this database holds phone numbers. The person table has only names (first, middle, last) and empty attribute columns, and party, location_address and the other tables have no phone or contact fields, so the phone number on file for Bob Agent cannot be determined.
Mary Policy Holder exists in the person table (Person_Identifier 1), but the Birth_Date column is NULL for her. The data does not record her date of birth.
Bob Agent exists in the person table (Person_Identifier 2), but Gender_Code is NULL for every person, so the database does not record Bob Agent's gender.

No table or column in the schema records occupation. The person table holds only names, birth date, gender and similar fields, and policy holders are linked through agreement_party_role to party and person. The only industry-type fields are in organizations, and the only organization is the insurer itself, so they say nothing about a policyholder's occupation.

The warehouse has no household income measure or attribute. The person table holds only names (and its other attributes are empty), party holds only identifiers, and the policy, claim and amount tables carry insurance amounts, not policyholder income. Nothing records the household income of a policyholder.

The database holds no marital status for anyone. The person table has only identifier, name parts, birth date, birth place, gender code and name affixes, and no other table has a marital status column. Only persons 1 to 3 have names filled in, and the other attributes are empty.

The warehouse holds no credit score. No table or column records a credit score or any pricing input. The assessment tables only link a policy to an underwriting assessment, whose result code is just 'OK'. Policy, policy_amount and premium hold only policy terms and amounts.

The warehouse only holds claims against this insurer (Mesa Underwriters Specialty Insurance Company), which is the only organization recorded. Claims have no insurer or prior-carrier field. The claim table's reported and claims-made dates are empty, and policy holders are linked to policies, not to claims filed elsewhere. Claims Mary Holder filed with other insurers before 2015 are therefore not in the data.

The warehouse has no repair estimate and no adjuster. Claim money in claim_amount is only classed as loss payment, loss reserve, expense payment or expense reserve, and Amount_Type_Code is empty. The party roles are only policy holder (PH), agent (AG) and underwriter (UW), so nothing records an adjuster or an approval. A loss reserve or loss payment would be a different measure from an adjuster-approved repair estimate.

answer.declineReason: No table or column records injuries or injured people. The claim table holds only identifiers, dates and a status code. claim_amount holds money amounts. occurrences has no injury or casualty field, and person only has names. The warehouse has no injury measure to count for claim 12312701.

Claim 12312702 exists (Claim_Identifier 2), but the data has no fraud flag or indicator for claims. Claim_Description, Claim_Status_Code and the other descriptive fields are empty. The assessment tables relate to policy underwriting, not claims, and their only result value is 'OK'. The catastrophe names are peril types such as Hurricane or Fire, not fraud markers.

The data has no attorney or litigation information. The only party roles are Agent (AG), Underwriter (UW) and PolicyHolder (PH), and no table links a claim to a party or records litigation. The claim, claim_amount and claim_coverage tables hold no legal-handling fields.

The data has no adjuster information. The only party roles are Agent (AG), Underwriter (UW) and PolicyHolder (PH). Party roles attach only to policies (agreement_party_role) and assessments (assesment_party_role), and no table links a party to a claim. Neither the claim table nor any other table has an adjuster or claim-handler attribute.

No table or column holds a claimant satisfaction rating or survey result. The claim table has only open and close dates and empty status fields. The only result-like field is assessment_result.Assessment_Result_Type_Code, which holds 'OK' for underwriting assessments of policies and has nothing to do with claimants or claims.

The data has no salvage measure. Claim money is only recorded as loss payment, loss reserve, expense payment and expense reserve, and Amount_Type_Code is empty, so no amount can be identified as salvage recovery. Claim 12312702 (Claim_Identifier 2) has only those four amounts: 2100 loss reserve, 2200 expense reserve, 2300 loss payment and 2400 expense payment. None of these is a salvage amount.

The data has no subrogation or recovery measure. Claim amounts are only marked as loss payments, loss reserves, expense payments or expense reserves, and Amount_Type_Code is empty. All 8 claim_amount rows are positive (1,000 to 2,400), so there are no recovery or negative amounts either. Any figure for claim 12312701 would be a different measure presented as subrogation.

Claim 12312701 (Claim_Identifier 1) has one loss payment, Claim_Amount_Identifier 3 for 1200, but the data holds no date for it. claim_amount.Event_Date is null, and the schema notes say a claim amount has no date of its own. The only dates on the claim are Claim_Open_Date (2019-01-15) and Claim_Close_Date (2019-01-31). Neither records when the payment was issued, so using either would substitute a different measure.

Claim 12312702 is Company_Claim_Number for Claim_Identifier 2. That claim has only one loss reserve row (Claim_Amount_Identifier 5, amount 2100), and its other three amounts are not loss reserves. claim_amount.Event_Date is empty, so no amount has a date, and there is no reserve history to break out by month. A month-by-month change in the loss reserve cannot be computed from this data.

The data has no currency information. claim_amount holds only a numeric Claim_Amount, with no currency code or column, and expense_payment only marks which claim amounts are expense payments. No other table records a currency, so the currency of the expense payment for claim 12312701 cannot be determined.

The data has no vendor or payee information. expense_payment holds only Claim_Amount_Identifier, and claim_amount has no payee or party column. The party and organizations tables hold no vendors; the only organization is the insurer itself. The data cannot show which vendor received the expense payment for claim 12312702.

The data has no industry-wide insured loss measure. Catastrophe.Industry_Catastrophe_Code is empty in every row, and the only loss amounts are this insurer's own claim amounts (claim_amount joined to loss_payment/loss_reserve). Those cover only the insurer's own claims linked to the Fire catastrophe, which is a different measure from total industry insured loss, so I did not substitute it.

The database has no wind speed or weather data. Occurrences hold only dates, and catastrophe holds only peril names like Hurricane or Tornado. Locations hold only addresses and coordinates. So the wind speed at the property for claim 12312701 cannot be determined.

The database has no rainfall or weather measure. The occurrences table only holds begin and end dates for the loss event, and its name, times, location and catastrophic-event indicator are empty. The catastrophe table holds only peril-type names such as Flood or Hurricane, not precipitation amounts. So the amount of rain during the occurrence behind claim 12312702 cannot be determined.

No table or column records flood zone designation for a property. Locations only hold a postal address and latitude/longitude. The catastrophe table has a 'Flood' peril name, but that labels a claim's event type, not whether the insured property lies in a flood zone, so it would be a different measure.

No table or column in this warehouse records property size or square footage. Insurable_object holds only identifiers and a location link, and location_address, geographic_location and pysical_location hold only address text, state, zip, and coordinates. The question cannot be answered without a measure that doesn't exist here.

No table or column in the database records roof material. The insurable_object table has an empty object type code, and the location tables hold only address, city, state, zip and coordinates. fire_claim has Fireplace and Year_Built but no roof attribute and cannot be joined to a property.

The location tables hold address and coordinates, and policy_coverage_detail has empty coverage and description codes. fire_claim has fireplace, year built and fire station data, but no sprinkler column, and it can't be joined to claims anyway. Whether the property in claim 12312701 has a sprinkler system is not recorded.

No table or column records smoke alarms. The insurable_object table has only an empty object type code and a location, location_address and pysical_location hold only address and coordinates, and fire_claim has a Fireplace flag but nothing on smoke alarms (and it can't be joined to claims anyway). The data cannot say whether the property in claim 12312702 has a smoke alarm.

No other table holds a property valuation, appraisal or assessed value.

Policy 31003000337 (Policy_Identifier 2) has a single term, 2019-06-01 to 2020-05-31, with one coverage detail and one premium of 12000.
